public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 233

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
  - [A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
  - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos233

/--
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233 :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^2 := by
  sorry

/--
Cramér proved an upper bound of $O(N(\log N)^4)$ conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233.variants.upper_bound (h : RiemannHypothesis) :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^4 := by
  sorry

/--
The prime number theorem immediately implies a lower bound of $\gg N(\log N)^2$ for the sum of
squares of gaps between consecutive primes.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/032848c62fdf4c422bb0ee6663dc8d009d456c2c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/233.lean#L57"]
theorem erdos_233.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun (N : ℕ) => N * (log N)^2) =O[atTop]
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos233

findings.description: The docstring reads "A conjecture by Heath-Brown: The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$." The Lean statement is only the upper bound `(fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n)^2) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^2`. That bound is Erdős's problem as posed on erdosproblems.com, so the Lean itself is correct. The docstring gets two things wrong. (1) It attributes the problem to Heath-Brown, but the cited source attributes it to Erdős ([Er40, p.440], [Er55c, p.2], [Er65b, p.205]). (2) "Behaves like" suggests an asymptotic or same-order statement. Heath-Brown's actual conjecture is the asymptotic $\sum_{p_n\le x} d_n^2 \sim 2x\log x$, i.e. $\sim 2N(\log N)^2$. That is strictly stronger than the O-bound the theorem states. So the docstring describes a different (stronger) claim than the Lean. The mathematics of the declaration is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/233 (snapshot web.archive.org/web/20260909151234): "Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Prove that \[\sum_{1\leq n\leq N}d_n^2 \ll N(\log N)^2.\]" with references [Er40,p.440] [Er55c,p.2] [Er65b,p.205]. OEIS A074741 FORMULA: "D. R. Heath-Brown's conjecture: Sum_{prime(n)<=N} (prime(n)-prime(n-1))^2 ~ 2*N*log(N)." erdosproblems forum thread 233: "On page 87 (just above Theorem 3) of 'Gaps between primes, and the pair correlation of zeros of the zeta-function' by Heath-Brown, he conjectures this same result but with the exact asymptotic constant 2."
findings.suggested_fix: State the problem as posed, e.g. "Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Prove that $\sum_{1 \le n \le N} d_n^2 \ll N(\log N)^2$." Heath-Brown's stronger asymptotic $\sum_{n \le N} d_n^2 \sim 2N(\log N)^2$ could be mentioned as a remark, or added as a separate variant. The Lean statement needs no change.

reformulations.difference: The source's Vinogradov bound $\sum_{1\le n\le N} d_n^2 \ll N(\log N)^2$ is stated as `IsBigO atTop` on ℕ, i.e. as an eventual bound. The sum is written as `∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n)^2`, where `primeGap n = nth Prime (n+1) - nth Prime n` is 0-indexed.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `Nat.nth Nat.Prime 0 = 2`, so `primeGap (k-1) = d_k` with the source's 1-indexed $p_1 = 2$. The Lean sum at N is therefore exactly $\sum_{1\le n\le N} d_n^2$ (checked in Lean at N = 1, 2, 3, 4 against OEIS A074741: 1, 5, 9, 25). For N ≥ 2 the right-hand side $N(\log N)^2$ is positive, so an eventual bound is equivalent to a bound for all N ≥ 2 with a larger constant. At N = 1 the right-hand side is 0 while the sum is 1, so the source can only mean large N (or N ≥ 2). `atTop` is the standard reading. The same reasoning applies to both variants.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/233 (via Wayback snapshot http://web.archive.org/web/20260909151234/https://www.erdosproblems.com/233; live site blocked by Cloudflare)
arXiv:1802.07609, Funkhouser–Goldston–Ledoan, 'Distribution of Large Gaps Between Primes' (LaTeX source: Cramér/Selberg conditional bound C(x) << x log^3 x under RH; expected C(x) ~ 2x log x)
could_not_verify: Erdos233.erdos_233.variants.lower_bound (only its formal_proof record): I did not open the linked proof at github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures (commit 032848c…). It is a fork of the formal-conjectures repository, which I was told not to consult. So I cannot confirm that the linked theorem is exactly this statement or that it is sorry-free. The statement itself is faithful to the source and mathematically true: by Cauchy–Schwarz, ∑_{n<N} d_n^2 ≥ (p_{N+1}−2)^2/N, and Chebyshev gives p_N ≫ N log N.

Primary papers (Erdős 1940/1955, Cramér 1936, Heath-Brown 1982): the PDFs I downloaded are image scans with no text layer, and no OCR was available. I relied on the erdosproblems.com wording (the file's primary source) and the FGL survey for the exact claims. This does not leave any statement's faithfulness unsettled.
review.notes:
No misformalizations found, and no status issues.

All three declarations elaborate as intended: `Real.log (↑N : ℝ)` (not `Nat.log`), real-valued sums, and `IsBigO` along `atTop` on ℕ.

- `erdos_233`: the upper bound O(N (log N)^2), which is exactly the erdosproblems.com statement. The problem is recorded as open on erdosproblems.com and in the teorth database, matching `research open`.
- `variants.upper_bound`: RH → O(N (log N)^4). Under RH, ∑_{p_{n+1}≤x} d_n^2 ≪ x log^3 x (Cramér 1936; see FGL), and p_N ≍ N log N turns this into O(N (log N)^4). It also follows directly from Selberg's ∑_{n≤N} d_n^2/n ≪ (log N)^4, since d_n^2 ≤ N·d_n^2/n. `research solved` is correct.
- `variants.lower_bound`: N (log N)^2 = O(sum), i.e. the source's ≫. It is true via Cauchy–Schwarz and Chebyshev.

Lean sanity checks:
- the sums at N = 1, 2, 3, 4 match OEIS A074741;
- primeGap n > 0, so the sum is ≥ N and the conjecture is not vacuous;
- the big-O unfolds to the standard ∃C, eventually |f| ≤ C|g| form.

The only defect found is the `erdos_233` docstring. It attributes the problem to Heath-Brown and says "behaves like", which describes Heath-Brown's stronger asymptotic conjecture (~2N(log N)^2) rather than the stated O-bound.

Other observations, not reported as findings:
- The module docstring cites OEIS as A74741 (unpadded). This is the repository-wide convention, used in 250+ links including the OEIS/ directory.
- The cited Wikipedia page (Cramér's conjecture) does not discuss the sum of squared gaps. It is a tangential reference.
- Selberg's RH-conditional refinement is not formalized. Leaving out a variant is not a misformalization.
